build: v127 Backend Opening Day Evidence Pack
downloadPurpose: Private backend repo opening-day evidence handoff before real GitHub execution.

evidenceLanes.label: Repo privacy proof
evidenceLanes.note: Screenshot or note proving the production backend repo is private before files move.

evidenceLanes.label: Setup command proof
evidenceLanes.note: Capture preflight, folder creation, starter file copy, install, and first quality command output.

evidenceLanes.label: Issue import proof
evidenceLanes.note: Backend issue bodies need issue URLs, labels, milestones, owners, and opening order evidence.

evidenceLanes.label: First PR proof
evidenceLanes.note: First PR needs scope note, linked issue, command proof, rollback note, risk reference, and owner review.

evidenceLanes.label: CI workflow proof
evidenceLanes.note: Planned workflow lanes need first run status, artifact names, and exact check labels.

evidenceLanes.label: Branch protection proof
evidenceLanes.note: Only apply required checks after real workflow names appear, then capture settings evidence.

evidenceLanes.label: Secret and data proof
evidenceLanes.note: Capture scan notes proving no live keys, customer files, or commercial fields entered the repo.

evidenceLanes.label: Signoff proof
evidenceLanes.note: Product, platform, backend, security, data, and QA owners need go/hold/no-go evidence.

captureChecklist.note: Screenshot or saved note confirms pursuitdesk-platform, private visibility, owner, and no-live-data scope.
Confirm no .env, live key, billing token, customer workbook, or certificate is in the copy set.
Capture apps, packages, infra, docs, scripts, workflows, env examples, and starter files in place.
Capture labels, milestones, board columns, and issue routing rules imported or intentionally deferred.
Capture first M0/M1 issue URLs with owner, label, milestone, proof command, and acceptance criteria.
Capture develop or feature branch creation and confirm main remains protected from direct work.
Capture PR title, scope, issue link, risk reference, proof checklist, rollback note, and reviewer list.
Capture install, lint/typecheck placeholder, route envelope placeholder, auth tenant placeholder, and release-gate notes.
Capture exact GitHub Actions check names that branch protection must later require.
Capture required checks, review requirement, conversation resolution, and admin bypass policy.
Capture artifacts, screenshots, logs, PR notes, signoffs, and open blockers in one folder.
Capture what passed, what remains placeholder, what is blocked, and what v128 execution checklist must enforce.

artifactFiles.note: Repo URL, visibility, owner, screenshot name, and no-live-data confirmation.
GitHub auth, git, node, package manager, and local environment checks.
Folder creation, starter file copy, and first command sequence transcript.
Issue URLs, labels, milestones, owners, and acceptance links.
PR scope, linked issue, proof commands, risk register link, rollback note, and review owners.
Actual workflow names, job names, status check labels, artifacts, and failure policy.
Manual scan notes for secrets, customer data, commercial values, and restricted files.
Protected branch settings, required checks, environment gates, and conversation resolution.
Product, platform, backend, security, data, and QA go/hold/no-go status.
What happened, what passed, what remains placeholder, blockers, and next build handoff.

proofCommands.note: Proves GitHub CLI account before private repo work starts.
Shows local file set before copying starter content into the private repo.
First dependency install proof or documented placeholder if repo shell is not executable yet.
Lint proof once package scripts exist; placeholder accepted only with clear next command.
Typecheck proof once TS shell exists; placeholder accepted only with issue link.
Route envelope tests prove safe response and request-id expectations.
Tenant isolation and section access command proof.
Aggregates checks, artifacts, blockers, owner decision, and rollback status.

screenshotPlan.note: Capture before files or issues are added.
Capture after first commit or PR branch push.
Capture label groups and priority/security/proof labels.
Capture opened issues filtered by first milestone.
Capture title, linked issue, checks area, and reviewers.
Capture job names, check names, artifacts, and failures if any.
Capture required checks only after workflow names are known.

prNoteSections.note: Create the backend shell and evidence path, not a full SaaS launch.
Root docs, API shell, packages, workflows, env examples, scripts, and evidence folder.
No live customer data, no live payment capture, no production hosting, no real imports.
Name the risk register and explain hard-stop, hold, and watch conditions.
List command outputs, placeholder reason, owner, and follow-up issue.
Add exact workflow and job names once GitHub Actions runs.
Delete branch, close PR, revert starter files, or rotate any exposed credential.
Product, platform, backend, security, data, and QA lanes with go/hold/no-go status.

workflowNameMap.proof: install, lint, typecheck, unit, contracts, routes, audit
auth tenant, redaction, denial audit, secret posture
login, records, commercial denial, import dry run, billing test mode, feedback
migration files, seed order, rollback, restore, source trace
artifact summary, blockers, owner decision, rollback proof
Configured only after actual workflow check names exist.

branchProtectionEvidence.note: Pull request required, direct pushes blocked, and conversation resolution enabled.
Names come from first workflow run, not guessed from file names.
Security, backend, platform, and data owners review their lanes.
Document whether admins can bypass and who can approve emergency merge.
CI artifacts and proof notes are saved for the first backend PR.
Rollback command, owner, and restore path are visible before merge.

signoffTrail.note: Approves controlled repo opening without approving live SaaS.
Confirms repo privacy, branch flow, setup sequence, and workflow check capture.
Confirms starter API, packages, scripts, and route proof expectations.
Confirms no secrets, no customer data, commercial redaction, tenant guard expectations.
Confirms only demo fixtures, source trace expectations, rollback path, and no real workbook import.
Confirms proof files, screenshots, command logs, PR notes, and open blocker summary.

acceptanceChecks.note: Eight lanes define what proof must be captured.
Twelve capture points cover before, during, and after repo opening.
Ten evidence files are named for the future private repo.
Eight commands define the first transcript expectations.
Eight screenshots cover repo, issues, PR, Actions, and branch protection.
Eight PR sections keep the first backend PR bounded.
Six branch-protection evidence items are required after CI names appear.
v128 can turn the evidence pack into a concrete private repo execution checklist.

handoff: v127 turns the runbook and risk register into an evidence pack for the first real private backend repo day.
The pack makes the future repo day auditable by naming proof files, screenshots, command transcripts, PR note sections, workflow names, branch-protection evidence, and owner signoffs.
The most important rule remains: capture private repo visibility, no-secret/no-live-data proof, first PR scope, and exact workflow check names before branch protection is finalized.
v128 can now convert this evidence plan into a concrete execution checklist that someone can follow line by line in GitHub.
